posts.cooked: I get the feeling more advanced players play on advance mode, so that skews things, but advanced players are (anecdotally) more likely to use the randomizer. How this evens out is anyone's guess.
posts.raw: I get the feeling more advanced players play on advance mode, so that skews things, but advanced players are (anecdotally) more likely to use the randomizer. How this evens out is anyone's guess.

posts.name: Estelindis
posts.cooked: Good point about more skilled players being more likely to take on tough challenges.  Not sure how data can adapt to this.  In a way, though, since advanced mode isn't supposed to be balanced play, it's probably less important to have a very accurate difficulty rating for it.  (Advanced mode does help to make the very easiest villains enjoyable again, though, so to me, it actually feels more balanced, just for those ones.)

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I hardly ever bother with advanced mode myself. It makes things harder, but it also adds more effects for me to forget every turn. The extra fiddliness isn't balanced by the extra fun for me.

And I'm not keen on advanced villains who just gain some DR. Just makes the game more of a slog, and can make heroes who do pingy damage feel useless. May as well throw that Hypersonic Assault in the trash then...
